title: JobFlow — a walkthrough
note: Each line is one TTS call (cached by voice + text). `say` is what the voice reads when it differs from the caption text.

lines: This is JobFlow, a job search engine that runs on your own computer.
It finds roles on company job boards, ranks them against your résumé, and tells you honestly how well you fit.
It helps you write your application from your own material, and it fills in the form. Then it stops, so you can check it and press submit.

lines.text: Setup takes a few minutes. Clone the repository, then run pnpm install and build.
lines.say: Setup takes a few minutes. Clone the repository, then run p-n-p-m install, and build.

lines.text: jobflow init reads your résumé — PDF, Word, LaTeX, Markdown or plain text — and asks you to confirm what it found.
lines.say: Then, jobflow in-it reads your résumé — PDF, Word, Lay-tek, Markdown or plain text — and asks you to confirm what it found.

lines: In the browser, the same setup is four short steps.
Every skill and every Evidence Bank item is copied from your résumé. You fix what's wrong, and nothing is made up.
Then you say where you can work, your pay floor, and the kinds of roles you want.
Next, a sync. JobFlow checks company job boards and public feeds. Here, it's a fictional demo set.
The panel shows each step as it runs, the boards being fetched, the jobs found so far, and roughly how long is left.
A board that doesn't answer is named, in plain words, and tried again next time.
Your jobs come back ranked for you.
Each card has a score, why it fits, and the likely gap — a language you haven't used, or more years than you have.
Pay is what the posting states, or an estimate that's labelled as one.
Flags call out the catches, like a post from a staffing agency, or a remote role that's open in one country only.

scenes.chapter: Filters that say what they hid
lines: Filters only hide. Scores never change, and the page tells you how many jobs a filter hid, and why.
Only two things are ever left out for you: pay stated below your floor, and a location you can't work from.
Open a job for the whole picture: how you fit, what to check before applying, and the full description.
Search asks the job boards right now, with the same honest scoring, and reports what your query hid.
Save a search, and it runs on every sync and becomes a tab on your Jobs page.
Tailor drafts a résumé, a cover letter and answers for one role.
They're built from your résumé, your Evidence Bank and your skills: rephrased and trimmed, never extended. Each draft says where it came from.
Without a model, you get your own résumé, reformatted, and cover letters are switched off rather than faked.

scenes.chapter: Apply: the checklist and the review gate
lines: The Apply checklist makes sure you have what you need: your name, your email and a résumé file.

lines.text: Then open the form yourself, or pre-fill it in a browser on your machine with jobflow apply --fill.
lines.say: Then open the form yourself, or pre-fill it in a browser on your machine, with jobflow apply, dash dash fill.

lines: It types only what you stored, attaches your résumé, and stops at the review screen.
JobFlow never submits. You read it, and you send it.
Once it's sent, mark it applied. Applications keeps every role from saved to offer, with a next step and a follow-up date.

scenes.chapter: From an AI agent, over MCP
lines: You can also use JobFlow from an AI assistant. jobflow mcp serves your local data over the Model Context Protocol.
The assistant can search, read a job, and plan an application as a dry run. It can't fill or submit a form.

lines.text: JobFlow is open source, under the AGPL. It runs on your machine, and your data stays there.
lines.say: JobFlow is open source, under the A-G-P-L. It runs on your machine, and your data stays there.

lines: Pick a style, light or dark. Use the terminal or the browser. And give it a try.
